subject: [PATCH v4 0/3] mm: zswap: free cold writeback folios promptly

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary: Reviewer Yosry Ahmed noted that a specific check in the code is no longer necessary because the return value 'ret' should always be non-zero, and suggested renaming the label to indicate it's only for error paths.
reviews.raw_body:
This check is now unneeded as ret should always be non-zero here, right?

We should probably also rename the label to indicate that it's only
the error path. Maybe "error" or "fail"?

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a swap cache folio is already on the LRU, and requested that the code be modified to check for this condition before attempting to drop the folio.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti agreed to the patch and gave a formal Reviewed-by tag.
reviews.raw_body:

2026-08-25.patch_summary: This patch series improves the performance of zswap by promptly freeing cold writeback folios instead of leaving them on the LRU for page reclaim to find and free later. The existing dropbehind mechanism is extended to swap cache folios, allowing zswap to opt into it. This change reduces memory residency and waste in reclaim scans. Patch 1 moves LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator, patch 2 drops dropbehind swap cache folios on writeback completion, and patch 3 enables zswap to allocate its writeback folio off the LRU and mark it as dropbehind.

reviews.author: Kunwu Chan
reviews.summary: Reviewer Kunwu Chan confirmed that the refcount handoff in v4 patch resolves his concern about overlapping references in zswap writeback.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks for addressing this.

I checked the refcount handoff in v4. Dropping the zswap reference before 
__swap_writepage() removes the refcount overlap I was concerned about in v3. 
The swapcache reference keeps the folio alive until writeback starts, and 
folio_end_writeback() takes the completion reference before clearing 
PG_writeback, so remove_mapping_reclaim() sees the expected refcount.

Reviewed-by: Kunwu Chan <kunwu.chan@gmail.com>

Thanks, 
KunWu

reviews.author: Kunwu Chan
reviews.summary: Reviewer Kunwu Chan noted that the new allocator contract is preserved by all callers of __swap_cache_alloc_folio(), but pointed out a discrepancy between regular swap-in paths and zswap writeback path, which keeps the folio off-LRU for dropbehind handling in patch 3.
sentiment_signals: discrepancy between swap-in paths and zswap
reviews.raw_body:
I checked the callers of __swap_cache_alloc_folio(). The regular 
swap-in paths add the folio to the LRU after allocation, while 
the zswap writeback path keeps it off-LRU for the dropbehind 
handling in patch 3. 
The new allocator contract is preserved by all callers.

swapfile.c still references the old name in a comment \u2014 minor
consistency nit.

Reviewed-by: Kunwu Chan <kunwu.chan@gmail.com>

Thanks,
KunWu

reviews.author: Kunwu Chan
reviews.summary: Reviewer Kunwu Chan confirmed that the extra reference in folio_end_writeback() provides the expected caller reference for remove_mapping_reclaim(), ensuring a correct refcount and preventing a racing swapin.
reviews.raw_body:
I checked the refcount handoff from folio_end_writeback() to
swap_writeback_dropbehind_folio(): the extra reference provides the
expected caller reference for remove_mapping_reclaim(), giving the
expected 1 + folio_nr_pages(folio) count for folio_ref_freeze().

The swapcache/dropbehind state is sampled before clearing PG_writeback,
and the extra reference keeps the folio alive across a racing swapin.

Reviewed-by: Kunwu Chan <kunwu.chan@gmail.com>

Thanks,
KunWu

reviews.author: Nhat Pham
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Nhat Pham expressed positive sentiment towards the patch, specifically praising the introduction of BIO_COMPLETE_IN_TASK infrastructure.

Reviewer Nhat Pham noted that the patch description does not explicitly mention what happens to the swap cache folio after it is marked dropbehind, and requested clarification on this point.

Reviewer Nhat Pham expressed confusion about the naming conventions used in remove_mapping_reclaim() and similar functions, but did not provide a concrete suggestion for improvement.
reviews.raw_body:
This BIO_COMPLETE_IN_TASK thing is really nice! I'm glad we have a
proper infra now and no longer have to roll our own solutions :)

---

[...]

I don't have a good suggestions for the naming...

(also I'm hoping we're fixing the weird shadows behavior of zswap
writeback soon :))

Anyway:
